numerical_failure.affected_api: numpy.ma.core._DomainedBinaryOperation.__call__ (masked array division via numpy.ma.core._DomainedBinaryOperation, mask calculation)
numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Masked array division with np.seterr(under='raise') raises an internal multiplication underflow FloatingPointError during mask calculation (issue #25810), even though the plain ndarray division x/2.0 works.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Masked array division should ignore all floating point errors in the mask calculation, so that X/2.0 completes without raising under np.errstate(under='raise').
trigger_conditions: the mask calculation multiplies np.finfo(float).tiny by absolute values, causing an underflow

input_output_examples.input: with np.errstate(under='raise'): X = np.ma.array(np.arange(0, 3, 0.1)); X2 = X/2.0
input_output_examples.buggy_output: underflow FloatingPointError raised from the mask calculation

oracle_clues: Fix changes np.errstate(invalid='ignore') to np.errstate(all='ignore') in the __call__ of the domained binary operation in numpy/ma/core.py
Proposed regression test test_masked_array_underflow in numpy/ma/tests/test_core.py uses np.errstate(under='raise') and checks X2 against x/2 (suggested np.testing.assert_array_equal(X2, x/2))
Original test assertion assert(X2.all() == X.all() / 2.0) was criticised because X.all() and X2.all() are both False

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: The mask calculation multiplies np.finfo(float).tiny by absolute values of the inputs, so the underflow arises at the smallest normal float magnitude; no other magnitude regime is stated.
numerical_characteristics.tolerance: The diff sets self.tolerance = np.finfo(float).tiny (smallest positive normal float64 value) in the domain-guard code path; no reproduction tolerance for comparisons is stated.
category_specific_evidence: Special value involved is underflow (FloatingPointError from np.errstate(under='raise')), not NaN, inf, signed zero or subnormals; the passages do not mention those other special values.
The mask computation umath.absolute(a) * self.tolerance >= umath.absolute(b) multiplies by np.finfo(float).tiny, which is where the underflow arises.
The fix in numpy/ma/core.py changes np.errstate(invalid='ignore') to np.errstate(all='ignore') in the masked division __call__, so all floating point errors are suppressed in that mask calculation.
The regression test test_masked_array_underflow uses x = np.arange(0, 3, 0.1), wraps X = np.ma.array(x), and checks np.testing.assert_array_equal(X2, x/2) under np.errstate(under='raise').
The draft assertion 'assert(X2.all() == X.all() / 2.0)' was questioned in review ('What does this assert test?') and is not a valid oracle.
The passages do not state the dtype, precision or a comparison tolerance; the dtype and tolerance fields are left null because the evidence is silent.
Buggy commit e191a5f38892 is given, but no PR date is stated in the passages.

Masked array division with np.seterr(under='raise') raises an internal multiplication underflow FloatingPointError during mask calculation (issue #25810), even though the plain ndarray division x/2.0 works.
Masked array division should ignore all floating point errors in the mask calculation, so that X/2.0 completes without raising under np.errstate(under='raise').
The diff sets self.tolerance = np.finfo(float).tiny (smallest positive normal float64 value) in the domain-guard code path; no reproduction tolerance for comparisons is stated.
The mask calculation multiplies np.finfo(float).tiny by absolute values of the inputs, so the underflow arises at the smallest normal float magnitude; no other magnitude regime is stated.
